items.q: Whipple triad with high insulin AND high C peptide during hypoglycaemia indicates what?
items.exp: Endogenous insulin secretion releases C peptide equally, so both rise inappropriately in insulinoma. Injected insulin contains no C peptide and suppresses endogenous release, lowering C peptide.
r: Incorrect. Injection suppresses C peptide.
Correct. Both high means the pancreas is over secreting.
Incorrect. Sulfonylureas also raise C peptide and must be screened separately.
Incorrect. Adrenal failure hypoglycaemia lacks hyperinsulinism.
items.kp: C peptide separates pancreas made from syringe given insulin.

items.q: MEN1 syndrome (menin loss) classically combines which three tumour sites?
o: Parathyroid, pituitary and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours
Lung, thymus and adrenal cortex only
items.exp: MEN1 is the three Ps: parathyroid hyperplasia (commonest first), pituitary adenomas and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours such as gastrinoma and insulinoma. MEN2 is the RET thyroid adrenal syndrome.
r: Incorrect. That medullary grouping is MEN2 territory.
Correct. Three Ps define MEN1.
Incorrect. Those are scattered associations, not MEN1 cores.
Incorrect. Those cancers follow other hereditary syndromes.
items.kp: MEN1 recites as parathyroid, pituitary, pancreas.

items.q: Refractory multiple peptic ulcers with diarrhoea and a pancreatic tumour suggest which hormone excess?
items.exp: Gastrinoma secretes gastrin driving massive acid, ulcers beyond the duodenal bulb, diarrhoea and inactivation of lipase. MEN1 screening follows because a fifth to a quarter associate.
r: Incorrect. Insulin excess causes hypoglycaemia, not ulcers.
Correct. Gastrin excess causes Zollinger Ellison ulcers.
Incorrect. Glucagonoma causes rash and diabetes instead.
Incorrect. Somatostatinoma causes gallstones and steatorrhoea triad.
items.kp: Ulcers that refuse to heal: measure gastrin.

items.q: Necrolytic migratory erythema with diabetes and weight loss points to which pancreatic tumour?
items.exp: Glucagonoma produces necrolytic migratory erythema, diabetes, weight loss, anaemia and thrombosis tendency from glucagon driven catabolism and amino acid depletion.
r: Incorrect. Insulinoma causes hypoglycaemia without this rash.
Correct. Rash plus diabetes means glucagonoma.
Incorrect. VIPoma causes watery diarrhoea and hypokalaemia (WDHA).
Incorrect. Somatostatinoma causes stones, diabetes and steatorrhoea.
items.kp: Migratory necrotic rash in diabetes: hunt glucagonoma.

items.q: Profuse watery diarrhoea with hypokalaemia and achlorhydria (WDHA) is caused by which tumour secretion?
items.exp: VIPoma secretes vasoactive intestinal peptide causing secretory diarrhoea litres daily, potassium loss and suppressed acid (pancreatic cholera). Octreotide controls secretion while locating tumour.
r: Incorrect. Gastrin raises acid, opposite pole.
Correct. VIP causes WDHA pancreatic cholera.
Incorrect. Insulin lowers glucose without secretory diarrhoea.
Incorrect. Calcitonin diarrhoea belongs to medullary cancer context.
items.kp: Secretory diarrhoea plus low potassium: VIPoma.

items.q: Earliest clinical marker of diabetic nephropathy progression is what?
o: Persistent microalbuminuria (raised urine albumin creatinine ratio)
items.exp: Diabetic kidney disease announces through persistent albuminuria (microalbuminuria) after hyperfiltration, years before filtration falls, making annual urine albumin screening and RAAS blockade timing decisive.
r: Incorrect. Haematuria suggests glomerulonephritis instead.
Correct. Microalbuminuria is the earliest marker.
Incorrect. Nephrotic ranges come late if at all.
Incorrect. Colic is stone disease, not diabetic nephropathy.
items.kp: Screen diabetic urine albumin yearly: earliest kidney signal.

items.q: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy threatens vision mainly through what?
o: New vessel growth causing vitreous haemorrhage and tractional detachment
items.exp: Ischaemic retina secretes VEGF growing fragile new vessels that bleed into vitreous and contract detaching retina. Laser and anti VEGF therapy target this neovascular drive.
r: Incorrect. Microaneurysms mark background disease.
Correct. New vessels bleed and detach retina.
Incorrect. Exudates threaten macula oedema vision differently.
Incorrect. Cotton wool spots are nerve fibre infarcts of earlier stage.
items.kp: New vessels are the blinding stage of diabetic eye disease.

items.q: Type 1 diabetes pathogenesis is best described as what?
o: Autoimmune T cell destruction of pancreatic beta cells with islet antibodies
items.exp: Type 1 diabetes is autoimmune insulitis destroying beta cells (GAD and other antibodies, HLA susceptibility), causing absolute insulin deficiency and ketosis proneness. Islet amyloid characterises type 2 instead.
r: Incorrect. Resistance defines type 2 physiology.
Correct. Autoimmune beta cell destruction causes type 1.
Incorrect. Islet amyloid accompanies type 2 diabetes.
Incorrect. Iron destruction is haemochromatosis bronze diabetes.
items.kp: Antibodies plus absolute deficiency equals type 1 diabetes.

items.q: Bronze diabetes with liver cirrhosis and arthropathy suggests pancreatic damage from what?
items.exp: Haemochromatosis deposits iron in pancreas (bronze diabetes), liver (cirrhosis), heart, joints and skin from HFE related hepcidin failure. Phlebotomy prevents progression if early.
r: Incorrect. Copper causes Wilson liver brain disease.
Correct. Iron overload causes bronze diabetes.
Incorrect. Insulitis is type 1 without bronze skin or cirrhosis pattern.
Incorrect. Alcohol calcifies pancreas exocrine mainly with malabsorption.
items.kp: Bronze skin plus diabetes plus cirrhosis: test iron and HFE.

items.q: Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state differs from ketoacidosis chiefly how?
o: Extreme hyperglycaemia and osmolality with minimal ketosis in type 2 elderly patients
items.exp: Hyperosmolar state retains enough insulin to suppress ketosis but not hyperglycaemia, causing profound dehydration and osmolality in elderly type 2 patients, often infection precipitated with high mortality.
r: Incorrect. Acidosis dominates DKA instead.
Correct. Huge glucose, high osmolality, few ketones.
Incorrect. Glucose is extremely high, not low.
Incorrect. It favours elderly type 2 patients.
items.kp: DKA has ketones and acid; HHS has osmolality and dryness.
